Article Title: 'Rahul's mohabbat ki dukan': BJP slams Congress' tributes to anti-Sikh riots accused Sajjan Kumar
Article Text:
Sajjan Kumar was sevring life imprisonment in Delhi's Tihar Jail

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Friday hit back at the Congress after several of its leaders paid tribute to former party leader Sajjan Kumar, a convict in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, who died at 80 Congress MP Deepender Hooda described the death of Kumar, a former three-term Lok Sabha MP, as an "irreparable loss.""Today, the country's political landscape has suffered an irreparable loss... Sajjan Kumar ji was a leader whose connection with people in Delhi and across north India was cited as a model across the country," he said.Reacting to Hooda's remarks, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress of "eulogising the killers of the Sikh community", referring to Kumar's role in the anti-Sikh riots."Congress calls late Sajjan Kumar, a man convicted in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, a 'role model'! How can Congress eulogise the killers of our Sikh community?" Bhandari posted on X."This is the real mindset of 'Mohabbat Ki Dukkan' (shop of love) of Rahul Gandhi and exposes the innate hate Congress has for the Sikh community!" Bhandari added, referring to a phrase used by Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha.The BJP spokesperson further demanded that Congress apologise for "insulting" the victims of the anti-Sikh riots and "rubbing" salt into the wounds of the survivors and victims' families.Congress leader Udit Raj also described Kumar's death as a "great loss" for the party."It is a great loss for the Congress. He was a very senior Congress leader, and it will be difficult to fill the void... He did a lot of work, especially for the poor," Raj stated.Sajjan Kumar died at Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital on Thursday."Sajjan Kumar was brought to Safdarjung Hospital by police with altered sensorium around 11 am. He was immediately admitted and resuscitation measures were initiated. Despite providing all necessary medical and life-support measures, he could not be saved and passed away at 12:30 pm," the hospital's statement read."He was a known case of high blood pressure and Parkinson's disease and had a history of multiple hospital admissions in the past," the statement added.Kumar was serving multiple life sentences after his conviction in cases linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi.He was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Delhi High Court on December 17, 2018, in a case related to the killing of five Sikhs and the burning of a gurdwara during the anti-Sikh riots.He was also sentenced to life imprisonment by a Delhi court in February 2025 in another case relating to the killing of two Sikh men during the riots.Kumar resigned from the primary membership of the Congress after the 2018 conviction.
Article Summary: Congress MP Deepender Hooda described the death of Kumar as an "irreparable loss" BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress of "eulogising the killers of the Sikh community" Kumar was serving multiple life sentences after his conviction in cases linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi.

Article Title: 'Meeting all about new ideas & perspectives': PM Modi after engaging with 'team Nabin' at party HQ
Article Text:
The meeting came days after the BJP announced its 65-member national team under party president Nitin Nabin.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday met the BJP ’s newly appointed team of national office-bearers at the party headquarters in the national capital and posed for a group photograph with them.Sharing pictures from the meeting on X, PM Modi said organisational meetings are an opportunity to exchange ideas and strengthen the party’s connect with people.“Organisational meetings are all about new ideas and perspectives aimed at strengthening the Party and deepening connect with the people. Great interaction with fellow Party colleagues and the new organisational team!” the Prime Minister said.The meeting was the first introductory interaction between PM Modi and the newly constituted national team, marking the beginning of the office-bearers’ new tenure.The meeting came days after the BJP announced its 65-member national team under party president Nitin Nabin. The new team includes 51 new faces and marks the party’s first major organisational reshuffle of this scale since 2015, when Amit Shah was BJP president.Former Rajasthan chief minister Vasundhara Raje Scindia and former RSS functionary Ram Madhav have been appointed national vice presidents, while former Union minister Smriti Irani is among the party’s eight national general secretaries.B L Santhosh has been retained as national general secretary (organisation), along with general secretaries Vinod Tawde and Sunil Bansal. The general secretary team also includes Biplab Kumar Deb, Gajendra Patel, Satish Poonia, Harish Dwivedi and Sanjay Bhatia.The new team has 12 women and six leaders from minority communities.Union minister Piyush Goyal has been reappointed as the BJP’s national treasurer. He had previously held the post before joining the Union Cabinet in 2014.Rajya Sabha MP Tarun Chugh has been appointed central office in-charge. Hemang Joshi of Gujarat will head the Yuva Morcha, while Roop Kumari Choudhary of Chhattisgarh will lead the Mahila Morcha.BJP MP Anil Baluni will continue as media convenor, with Ashish Usha Agrawal, Pradeep Bhandari and Siddharth Yadav as co-convenors. Deepak Mhaskey of Chhattisgarh has been appointed social media convenor.Earlier in the day, Nabin held his first meeting with the newly appointed national office-bearers to discuss preparations for upcoming assembly elections and plans to strengthen grassroots outreach, party sources said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi met the BJP ’s newly appointed team of national office-bearers. The meeting came days after the BJP announced its 65-member national team under party president Nitin Nabin. The new team includes 51 new faces and marks the party’s first major organisational reshuffle of this scale since 2015.

Article Title: Rs 5 crore to suppress rape case? NHRC directs Punjab to probe allegations against CM Mann’s wife
Article Text:
NHRC takes cognisance of complaint against Bhagwant Mann's wife

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Human Rights Commission ( NHRC ) on Saturday took cognisance of allegations that Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann ’s wife Gurpreet Kaur sought Rs 5 crore to "suppress" a rape case The NHRC has directed the Punjab chief secretary and director general of police (DGP) to inquire into the allegations and submit an Action Taken Report (ATR) within two weeks.Commission member Priyank Kanoongo noted the complainant in the matter is a former judge of the Punjab and Haryana high court.“We have received a complaint from former Punjab and Haryana High Court Justice Ranjit Singh alleging that the wife of Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann attempted to hush up a rape case in exchange for a bribe of Rs 5 crore. ,” Kanoongo told ANI.Kanoongo further stated that the NHRC had also apprised the ministry of home affairs (MHA) of the allegations.“We will be able to proceed with further investigation only after receiving the report from the Punjab chief secretary and DGP. Officials should exercise the powers granted to them by the Constitution for the welfare of the people. If they act under any kind of political pressure, action can be taken against them,” he added.This comes days after the NHRC, on August 19, took cognisance of a complaint concerning the alleged non-observance of Independence Day in government schools across Punjab and sought a detailed report from the Mann-led state government.The complaint raised specific concerns about government schools in rural, remote and border areas, where Independence Day celebrations were allegedly not held. This, the complaint argued, may have deprived students of an opportunity to participate in national celebrations.In this matter, the Punjab chief secretary has been directed to submit a detailed Action Taken/Compliance Report within four weeks. The commission has also sought relevant information from the Ministry of Education and apprised the Union home ministry for appropriate action.The NHRC is seeking to determine whether children in border areas were denied equal opportunities to participate in the observance of the national festival solely because of the geographical location of their schools.
Article Summary: NHRC takes cognisance of complaint against Bhagwant Mann's wife Gurpreet Kaur. Commission member Priyank Kanoongo noted the complainant in the matter is a former judge of the Punjab and Haryana high court. The NHRC has directed the Punjab chief secretary and director general of police to inquire into the allegations and submit an Action Taken Report.

Article Title: ​​Former Sena minister Sattar holds closed-door discussion with Jarange
Article Text:
Former Shiv Sena minister Abdul Sattar (right) with quota activist Manoj Jarange

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Former minister and Sillod MLA Abdul Sattar on Saturday met Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange at Antarwali Sarathi in Jalna district, holding a closed-door discussion for nearly an hour ahead of Jarange’s proposed agitation from Aug 29.The meeting assumes significance as Jarange has recently intensified attacks on deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde and other Mahayuti politicians over the Maratha reservation issue, accusing govt of failing to honour its promises.However, Sattar sought to downplay political speculation surrounding the visit. “I have come here as a friend, not as a politician. Manoj Jarange is my friend. I came to meet him personally,” he said.Sattar, considered close to Shinde, said Jarange raised several issues concerning Maratha reservation and farmers during the discussion. “I will convey the demands directly to the chief minister and both deputy CMs. My request is that my visit should not be politicised,” he said.Jarange, meanwhile, reiterated that the Aug 29 agitation would go ahead unless govt addressed key demands of the Maratha community.“Govt should hand over us data showing that 58 lakh Kunbi certificates were issued in the first place.I am talking of issuing certificates and not merely finding Kunbi records. Those who have applied for Kunbi certificates or caste validity certificates must get certificates before Aug 28,” he said.The quota activist accused govt of failing to act despite being given ample time. “Instead of taking concrete actions, you are betraying us,” he said.Jarange recently targeted Shinde over the reservation issue and also criticised Sena minister Sanjay Shirsat and BJP minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule.Notably, Sattar is not the first senior Sena functionary to reach out to Jarange. Industries Minister Uday Samant had also met the activist in April amid efforts to engage with the ongoing reservation movement.
Article Summary: Former minister and Sillod MLA Abdul Sattar met Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange at Antarwali Sarathi in Jalna district. The meeting assumes significance as Jarange has recently intensified attacks on deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde and other Mahayuti politicians over the Maratha reservation issue.

Article Title: Ambernath BJP-MNS clash: Case registered against 2 BJP corporators, five others
Article Text:
A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash.





AMBERNATH: The political clash between BJP and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers in Ambernath has taken a fresh turn, with Shivaji Nagar police registering a fresh case against seven people, including two BJP corporators, on the complaint of an MNS worker who was injured in the incident.The latest case was registered on Sunday on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash. Police have booked BJP corporators Abhijit Karanjule and Pawan Walekar along with five others under sections 118(1), 115(2), 189(2), 190, 191(2) and 324(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The development comes days after police arrested Shirke and some of his associates for allegedly assaulting BJP office-bearer Laxmi Narayan Chauhan at his office in Vadavali.A subsequent clash between BJP and MNS workers at Shivaji Nagar police station further escalated tensions.MNS leaders had alleged that police took one-sided action by arresting their office-bearers while failing to act against BJP workers allegedly involved in the assault on Shirke. MNS leader Avinash Jadhav had demanded action against those responsible.Following the demand, MNS district president Bandu Deshmukh had announced a protest on Sunday against what the party termed one-sided police action. However, after police registered an FIR against BJP workers, MNS withdrew its protest.
Article Summary: A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash. The latest case was registered on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash.

Article Title: Four bus passengers injured after MSRTC bus hits stationary private bus near Chakan
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





Four passengers travelling in an MSRTC bus sustained injuries after the bus rammed into a stationary private bus at Chakan on Friday morning.Chakan North police registered a case lodged by the bus conductor against the MSRTC bus driver for negligent driving.An officer from Chakan North police said, “Three women passengers and a male passenger sustained minor injuries in the accident. It happened around 10.30am when the bus was travelling from Pune to Nashik. When the bus reached near Talegaon Chowk in Chakan, the driver noticed a private bus halted along the Pune-Nashik highway. When he tried to stop the bus, its brakes failed and it hit the stationary private bus.”
Article Summary: Chakan North police registered a case lodged by the bus conductor against the MSRTC bus driver for negligent driving. It happened around 10.30am when the bus was travelling from Pune to Nashik. When the bus reached near Talegaon Chowk in Chakan, the driver noticed a private bus halted.

Article Title: Man gets 20-years’ RI for sexually assaulting minor
Article Text: Chandrapur: District and Sessions Judge PM Gupta sentenced a 30-year-old man to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment and levied a 5,000 fine for sexually assaulting a five-year-old girl in Vandra, Brahmapuri taluka, in 2022. Court further ordered the fine amount be paid to the victim as compensation.The incident occurred at the Gurukunj Ashram temple premises in Vandra between 10.15am and 11am on August 27, 2022. According to prosecution, the minor was playing in the premises when the accused, Yuvraj Meshram sexually assaulted her. The complainant rushed to the spot as the girl raised an alarm. Meshram was seen fleeing the spot after the incident.Brahmapuri police registered a case under Section 376(AB) of IPC and Sections 6 and 10 of POCSO Act and arrested Meshram. IO PSI Swati Phulekar collected witness statements, medical evidence and other circumstantial evidence before filing the chargesheet.Public Prosecutor Sudhakar Degawar represented prosecution. Court accepted the prosecution's evidence and convicted Meshram under Section 6 of POCSO Act. In default of payment of the fine, the accused was also sentenced to one month of simple imprisonment.
Article Summary: The incident occurred at the Gurukunj Ashram temple premises in Vandra, Brahmapuri taluka, in 2022. Yuvraj Meshram was seen fleeing the spot after the incident. Court accepted the prosecution's evidence and convicted Meshram under Section 6 of POCSO Act.

Article Title: Senthilbalaji appears for inquiry in Tasmac irregularities case
Article Text: Chennai: Former minister V Senthilbalaji appeared before the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) in Alandur on Saturday for questioning in connection with a case involving alleged irregularities in the functioning of Tasmac. Investigators questioned him about the alleged irregularities, documents collected during the searches and his links with the other accused.The DVAC FIR names Senthilbalaji, former Tasmac managing director S Vishakan, former senior regional managers Rama Durai and Panneerselvam, and three associates of Senthilbalaji. On July 29, DVAC teams conducted searches at 41 locations.
Article Summary: V Senthilbalaji appeared before the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) in Alandur on Saturday. Investigators questioned him about the alleged irregularities, documents collected during the searches and his links with the other accused. On July 29, DVAC teams conducted searches at 41 locations.

Article Title: Assaulted by gang, youth dies at GH; four arrested so far
Article Text:
Murdered over relationship

Chennai:





Four persons have been arrested so far in connection with the murder of a 22-year-old person over a relationship issue at Thaiyur near Kelambakkam.The deceased, Praveen Kumar of Chinnamma Nagar, Thaiyur, had been in a relationship with a woman from the same locality for three years. Her family opposed the relationship. On Aug 16, a group of men attacked Praveen with machetes near his house. He was admitted to a private hospital in Kelambakkam and later shifted to Rajiv Gandhi Govt General Hospital, where he died during treatment on Aug 20.Kelambakkam police initially registered a case of attempt to murder based on a complaint from Praveen’s mother, Parvathi, 48. After his death, the case was altered to murder under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Police, ruling out an honour killing angle in the murder, said already they have had arrested S Ezhumalai, 43, his son E Gowtham, 18, and M Nandhees, 18, and R Manikandan, 32. E Gowtham, was arrested on Friday. All four were remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Praveen Kumar of Chinnamma Nagar, Thaiyur, had been in a relationship with a woman from the same locality for three years. Her family opposed the relationship. On Aug 16, a group of men attacked Praveen with machetes near his house.

Article Title: HC quashes criminal case against students who protested against anti-Sanatan Dharma meet
Article Text:
HC quashes FIR against students





Madurai: Madras high court quashed criminal cases registered against students who had protested against the conduct of the Sanatan Dharma eradication conference in Madurai district in 2023.“The petitioner and others raised their agitation in a peaceful and democratic manner and further, there is no allegation of any damage to any public property,” said Justice R Vijayakumar, quashing the case.He also observed that the petitioner and others, who belonged to a students association, had conducted a protest in front of a conference hall, where a meeting was conducted for eradication of Sanatan Dharma. In such circumstances, continuation of the criminal proceedings would only be an abuse of process of law.The other accused persons also stand on the same footing, the judge observed and quashed the FIR not only as against the petitioner, but also against other persons.The court was hearing a petition filed by M Senthoorvelan seeking to quash the FIR registered against him by the Tallakulam police in Madurai in 2023.The case of the prosecution is that the petitioner along with seven others belonging to a students association staged a protest against the conduct of a conference for eradication of Sanatan Dharma. Despite warnings given by police, he and others blocked the road and caused inconvenience to the general public.Counsel submitted that the petitioner was a student of law and that he had raised his objection with regard to the conduct of such a meeting. Noting that they had peacefully protested in front of the conference hall, he said it could not be considered to be an offence.On his part, the govt advocate submitted that though the charge sheet was ready, it has not been filed before the court so far.
Article Summary: Madras high court quashes criminal cases registered against students who had protested against the conduct of the Sanatan Dharma eradication conference in Madurai district in 2023. “The petitioner and others raised their agitation in a peaceful and democratic manner and further, there is no allegation of any damage to any public property,” said Justice R Vijayakumar.

Article Title: Paramakudi DSP suspended after wife’s harassment complaint
Article Text:
Paramakudi deputy superintendent of police (DSP) Y Jaffer Siddique was placed under suspension on Friday following a complaint by his wife alleging harassment over his alleged extramarital affair.

Madurai

:





Paramakudi deputy superintendent of police (DSP) Y Jaffer Siddique was placed under suspension on Friday following a complaint by his wife alleging harassment over his alleged extramarital affair.According to sources, when Siddique was serving in the Vellore region, his wife lodged a police complaint alleging that he was in an extramarital relationship and harassed her when she questioned him. Vellore district police subsequently registered a case against him.On Friday, a CB-CID investigating officer questioned Siddique at Paramakudi. He was later placed under suspension. Further investigation is underway.In a separate case, the Tirunelveli All Women Police registered a case on Friday against Arunkumar, inspector of Veeravanallur police station, for allegedly harassing a woman with whom he was in an extramarital relationship. He was subsequently placed under suspension.
Article Summary: Paramakudi deputy superintendent of police (DSP) Y Jaffer Siddique was placed under suspension on Friday following a complaint by his wife. Siddique's wife lodged a police complaint alleging that he was in an extramarital relationship and harassed her when she questioned him.

Article Title: Two riders killed after bike rams into steel railing in Madurai district
Article Text:
AIADMK cadres led by former minister R Kamaraj protest in Trichy against the TVK govt over not waiving off agricultural loans and indifference shown on the Mekkadatu issue and failing to protect state water rights.





Madurai: Two men were killed after their two-wheeler collided with a roadside steel railing near Chinna Udaippu village in Madurai district on Saturday.Police identified the deceased as M Pandidurai, 22, and M Muneeswarar, 21, residents of Aruppukottai in Virudhunagar district. They were working as construction workers in Thiruppalai in Madurai district. On Saturday morning, they were travelling on a two-wheeler to attend a temple festival at their native place, police said.When they were near Chinna Udaippu village, their vehicle rammed into a roadside steel railing. Both Pandidurai and Muneeswarar died on the spot, police said.Avaniyapuram police sent the bodies to Govt Rajaji Hospital for postmortem. They registered a case and are investigating.
Article Summary: M Pandidurai, 22, and M Muneeswarar, 21, were working as construction workers in Thiruppalai in Madurai district. On Saturday morning, they were travelling on a two-wheeler to attend a temple festival at their native place. Their vehicle rammed into a roadside steel railing.

Article Title: Former sub-registrar held in Meenakshi temple land case
Article Text:
Central Crime Branch (CCB) police have arrested former sub-registrar Anantharaman in connection with the alleged transferring and registering of Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple property worth around Rs60 crore.





Madurai: Central Crime Branch (CCB) police have arrested former sub-registrar Anantharaman in connection with the alleged transferring and registering of Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple property worth around Rs60 crore. It was the sixth arrest made by CCB in the case.According to police, a fraudulent patta transfer, allegedly carried out in 2016, was cancelled following objections. While related litigation was pending before Madras high court , a fresh document allegedly concealing key facts was registered at the Murappanadu sub-registrar office in 2021.Police investigations revealed that power deeds registered at Murappanadu and Vadamadurai sub-registrar offices played a crucial role in the alleged fraud. These power documents were allegedly used as the basis for subsequent registrations that facilitated the disputed property transactions.Anantharaman, who served as sub-registrar at Murappanadu when the disputed documents were registered, was taken into custody and remanded to judicial custody after being produced before a court on Thursday.CCB registered a case and is investigating 19 accused in connection with the fraud.Several people, including Rajkumar, Ilaiyaraja, then VAO Arasan, Kalikumar, and then tahsildar Anbalagan have already been arrested. Anbalagan was also placed under suspension following his arrest.Police are continuing their probe into the chain of transactions, including registration of power deeds and subsequent alleged fraudulent documents linked to the trust properties. The disputed property comprises Ashoka Villas bungalow and a two-acre garden located near Tallakulam-Alagarkovil Road.
Article Summary: Central Crime Branch (CCB) police have arrested former sub-registrar Anantharaman in connection with the alleged transferring and registering of Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple property worth around Rs60 crore. It was the sixth arrest made by CCB in the case.

Article Title: Lady doctor arrested near Salem for illegal fetal gender determination
Article Text: SALEM: Police on Wednesday arrested a lady doctor in Vazhapadi in Salem district on charges of illegally determining and disclosing the gender of fetuses to pregnant women. Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running in the area. They sealed the clinic.Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child.Acting on a complaint, a team led by joint director Dr S P Nandhini, Attur district health officer Dr N Yoganand and Vazhapadi Government Hospital chief medical officer Dr Ramesh Kumar raided the facility.They found that Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had received Rs 30,000 from a pregnant woman to determine the gender of her fetus. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.Health department officials said this was not the first violation by the clinic. It had been raided twice earlier, and Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had faced restrictions on conducting scans and treatments, they said. Cases were registered against her then too.
Article Summary: Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running. Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.

Article Title: Probe ordered into Onam celebration by ED-attack case accused
Article Text:
Thiruvananthapuram

:





The ADGP (law and order) has ordered an inquiry into the Onam celebrations and reel-making allegedly involving accused persons in the Enforcement Directorate (ED) attack case outside the Museum police station in Thiruvananthapuram.The special branch assistant commissioner has been asked to ascertain whether there was any lapse on the part of police personnel in allowing the accused, who are CPM leaders, to conduct the celebrations and shoot reels in front of the station. The ADGP has directed that strict action be taken if any negligence is established.The celebrations and reel shoot were reportedly led by former CPM councillor and ED attack case accused I P Binu. The accused were seen shooting reels while sitting on a swing arranged by police in front of the station. The swing had been installed near the floral decoration prepared by police as part of the Onam celebrations.Police have also initiated steps to approach the court seeking cancellation of Binu’s bail.
Article Summary: The ADGP (law and order) has ordered an inquiry into the Onam celebrations and reel-making allegedly involving accused persons in the Enforcement Directorate (ED) attack case. The special branch assistant commissioner has been asked to ascertain whether there was any lapse on the part of police personnel.

Article Title: Arjun Ayanki gets bail in cybercrime case
Article Text:
Arjun Ayanki

Kannur

:





Thalassery chief judicial magistrate court on Saturday granted bail to Arjun Ayanki, who is accused in multiple cases, including gold robbery. The bail was granted in a case registered by Kannur cybercrime police. However, he will continue in jail as he is accused in other criminal cases and Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (Kaapa) was invoked against him.The Kaapa order was issued based on a recommendation submitted by Kannur city police commissioner to the district collector. According to the order, Arjun poses a threat to society and there is a possibility that he may be involved in more criminal activities if he is released on bail.Now, Arjun is in judicial custody, and the police will formally record a fresh arrest of the accused based on the Kaapa order. Later, he will be sent to Kannur Central jail.
Article Summary: Arjun Ayanki is accused in multiple cases, including gold robbery. The bail was granted in a case registered by Kannur cybercrime police. He will continue in jail as he is accused of other criminal cases. Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (Kaapa) was invoked against him.

Article Title: Palakkad MP opposes move splitting railway division
Article Text:
VK Sreekandan

Palakkad

:





Congress MP V K Sreekandan has strongly criticised the move to exclude Mangaluru from Palakkad railway division, alleging that the decision was taken without informing Kerala MPs or the state govt.Calling it a ‘midnight move’ aimed at appeasing BJP in Karnataka , Sreekandan said the decision amounted to a blatant violation of the assurance given by the railway minister that Palakkad division would not be split.“Neither the MPs from Kerala nor the state govt was informed about this decision. This midnight move is clearly aimed at appeasing the BJP in Karnataka,” Sreekandan said.He alleged that removing Mangaluru from Palakkad division would reduce its revenue and allocation of funds and eventually weaken the division.“Centre is trying to destroy Palakkad division by reducing its revenue and funds. This is an anti-people move,” he said.Sreekandan warned that strong protests would be organised against the railway authorities’ decision. “We will continue the fight against the anti-people decision and raise the issue strongly both inside and outside Parliament,” he said.
Article Summary: Congress MP V K Sreekandan has strongly criticised the move to exclude Mangaluru from Palakkad railway division. He alleges that the decision was taken without informing Kerala MPs or the state govt. ‘We will continue the fight against the anti-people decision and raise the issue strongly both inside and outside Parliament,’ he said.

Article Title: Measure material desilted from Chulliyar dam in the presence of Palakkad district geologist: Kerala HC
Article Text:
Kochi





: The high court has directed Kerala Irrigation Infrastructure Development Corporation (KIIDC) to ensure that the quantity of desilted material from the Chulliyar dam in Palakkad is measured in the presence of the district geologist, Palakkad, to prevent excess material from being removed from the dam, which could cause significant loss to the state exchequer.A bench of Justice A A Ziyad Rahman issued the directive on a petition filed by M/s Koothradans Infrastructure LLP, the contractor entrusted with the desiltation work at Chulliyar dam, seeking transit passes to remove the extracted desilting sediments, consisting of sand, clay and waste oil, from the dam.During the previous hearing on Aug 3, the KIIDC submitted that although the petitioner had been permitted to desilt 11,33,610 cubic metres of sediments, 2,25,830.17 cubic metres of the desilted material remained to be disposed of and was stacked at the site and its premises. It was further submitted that although the contract period had already expired, the corporation had no objection to transporting the material already desilted, for which the petitioner had already paid royalty. Accordingly, the court directed the KIIDC to make necessary arrangements to measure the quantity of desilted sediments lying on the dam premises and, upon completion of the measurement, issue the necessary transit passes to the petitioner for transporting the material.However, on Aug 20, a third party filed an impleading petition alleging that the quantity of material kept on the dam premises after excavation was much more than what was specified in the statement submitted by the KIIDC. The impleading petitioner also sought the appointment of an advocate commissioner to measure the quantity, alleging that the contractor and certain KIIDC officials were acting in collusion to extract and remove excess material from the premises. Accordingly, the bench suo motu impleaded the district geologist, Palakkad, in the petition to monitor the measurement procedure and adjourned the matter to Sept 25.
Article Summary: Kerala Irrigation Infrastructure Development Corporation (KIIDC) ordered to measure the quantity of desilted material from the Chulliyar dam in Palakkad. A third party filed an impleading petition alleging that the quantity kept on the dam premises after excavation was much more than what was specified in the statement submitted by KIIDC.

Article Title: Murder case accused detained under Kaapa
Article Text:
Kochi

:





A 48-year-old murder case accused has been detained under Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (Kaapa) and lodged in Viyyur Central Jail.Betin of Sebipuram, Manjapra, was detained on the orders of district collector Priyanka G based on a report submitted by Ernakulam rural district police chief K S Sudarshan.According to the police, Betin is accused in several cases, including murder, trespassing, unlawful assembly, criminal intimidation and theft. He is the sixth accused in the case relating to the murder of Ashiq Manoharan in Angamaly in Oct 2024.He was detained under Kaapa for six months in early 2025.
